title: ML-MT124-ValidationHandoff

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the validation handoff — what Handshake does mechanically when an MT run enters VALIDATION_HANDOFF (worker signaled READY_FOR_VALIDATION / MT_IMPLEMENTED / PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE). This productizes the operator's per-MT validator step: today the orchestrator relays 'coder done' to a validator session by hand; here Handshake either notifies the orchestrator model or auto-spawns a validator worker, per policy, and the validator's own structured exit closes the run.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: One new backend module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/mt_validation_handoff.rs (policy type, hook subscription to state-change events, orchestrator notification path, validator auto-spawn path, closure application, receipts), wired into swarm_orchestration/mod.rs; tests.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Policy — pub enum ValidationHandoffPolicy { NotifyOrchestrator, AutoSpawnValidator { validator_role_id: String, lane_pin: Option<String> } } carried per-dispatch (from MtDispatchPolicy in MT-122) with a coordinator-level default. Policy is data, not code: both paths always record receipts.
2. Trigger — subscribe to MT-123 state-change events on the MT-009 bus; on transition INTO ValidationHandoff for run R: load the run + the implementer's full MtSignal (from session transcript/FR by signal_payload_sha256) + the original MicrotaskContractDoc (from the dispatch record's payload provenance).
3. Path A: NotifyOrchestrator — deliver a typed validation-request notification through the MT-105 notification surface to the orchestrator session that owns the dispatch (parent attribution from MT-101 spawn lineage). Notification payload: run_id, wp_id, mt_id, implementer session_id, signal kind, evidence summary, changed_paths, disclosure notes if PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE. NO POLLING: this is push through the existing mechanical notification path; the orchestrator model then drives validation itself (e.g. via the MT-101 spawn tool) and reports closure through the closure API below.
4. Path B: AutoSpawnValidator — spawn a validator worker via the MT-101 governed spawn path (which itself routes through SwarmCoordinator — no new spawn path), role_id = validator_role_id (validator child-role per MT-086), input payload composed via MT-083 with sections: (a) validator role overlay; (b) the ORIGINAL MT contract (verbatim scope/acceptance_criteria/proof_targets); (c) the implementer's MtSignal verbatim (evidence, changed_paths, notes); (d) OUTPUT FORMAT = hsk.mt_signal@1 (validator's required structured exit); (e) instruction that the validator verdict semantics are role-contextual: signal MT_IMPLEMENTED = VALIDATION_PASSED, FAILED = VALIDATION_REJECTED, BLOCKED/NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF = validation impossible (typed blocker). This role-contextual mapping is a DECLARED convention of this MT (hsk.mt_signal@1 deliberately has no separate validator vocabulary in v1) and MUST be written into the validator role overlay and the receipts.
5. Closure — pub fn apply_validation_closure(run_id, validator_signal: MtSignal, closer: ClosureActor) applying: PASSED -> MT-123 transition VALIDATION_HANDOFF->VALIDATED; REJECTED -> ->FAILED{ValidatorRejected} (validator's evidence/notes stored as rejection detail); blocker signals -> ->FAILED{ValidatorRejected} is WRONG — they map to run staying resolvable: apply ->BLOCKED{blocker} so an operator/orchestrator re-decision is possible. ClosureActor records WHO closed (validator session_id or orchestrator report) for attribution. Closure is idempotent via MT-123's idempotency keys.
6. Receipts BOTH directions — (a) handoff receipt at dispatch of the validation request: { receipt_id, run_id, policy, target (orchestrator session or validator session_id), issued_at_utc, implementer_signal_sha256 }; (b) closure receipt at verdict application: { receipt_id, run_id, verdict, validator_signal_sha256, closer, closed_at_utc }. Both persisted per the crate's receipt conventions and emitted as events (MT-009 bus + FR kinds reserved by MT-161).

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read the MT-105 notification surface, MT-101 spawn-tool surface, MT-086 role definitions, and MT-123's event payloads in the product worktree; match conventions.
2. Implement ValidationHandoffPolicy + the event subscription trigger (dedupe on run_id: at-most-one handoff per run, guarded by MT-123's single-entry VALIDATION_HANDOFF invariant plus a local receipt-existence check).
3. Implement Path A notification with full typed payload; test with a recording notification sink.
4. Implement Path B auto-spawn via MT-101/MT-083; test with the fake-lane pattern; assert the composed validator payload contains contract + implementer signal verbatim and the verdict-semantics instruction.
5. Implement apply_validation_closure with the verdict mapping above + both receipts; assert receipts and events with RecordingSwarmSink.
6. Negative tests: duplicate handoff trigger (second event for same run) produces no second spawn/notification; validator emitting a malformed signal -> SignalParseFailure recorded, run NOT closed, handoff receipt remains open (surfaced for MT-125/operator); closure for a run not in VALIDATION_HANDOFF -> IllegalTransition surfaced.
7. Run proof targets.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (legacy React; GUI surface exception exists only on the board MT MT-125)
.GOV/** (the product READS MT contracts; it never writes .GOV)
acceptance_criteria: Entering VALIDATION_HANDOFF triggers exactly ONE handoff action per run (dedupe proven by duplicate-event test).

NotifyOrchestrator path delivers a typed validation-request notification through the MT-105 surface to the attributed parent orchestrator session, carrying run_id/wp_id/mt_id/implementer signal summary — push, zero polling.

AutoSpawnValidator path spawns ONLY via the MT-101 governed spawn path with the validator role; the composed payload contains the original MT contract and the implementer's signal verbatim plus the hsk.mt_signal@1 output requirement and the declared verdict-semantics mapping — asserted by test.

Validator closure applies the mapping: MT_IMPLEMENTED->VALIDATED, FAILED->FAILED{ValidatorRejected} with stored rejection detail, BLOCKED/NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF->BLOCKED{blocker}; PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE from a validator is rejected as an invalid verdict (typed error) — all covered by tests.
Receipts recorded BOTH directions (handoff receipt + closure receipt) with payload hashes and actors, and each emits an event on the swarm bus/FR path.
Malformed validator signal NEVER closes a run: SignalParseFailure recorded, run state unchanged, receipt remains open — negative test.
cargo build -p handshake_core green; new tests green.
expected_tests: single-handoff dedupe on duplicate trigger events
Path A notification payload completeness via recording sink
Path B validator payload verbatim-content + governed-spawn-only assertions
verdict mapping matrix incl. invalid validator verdicts
malformed validator signal leaves run open with typed failure recorded
implementation_notes: The verdict-semantics mapping (validator MT_IMPLEMENTED == VALIDATION_PASSED) is a v1 economy decision: one signal schema for all workers keeps transports (MT-027/046/ACP) single-schema. If refinement later adds hsk.validation_verdict@1, this module is the only place the mapping lives — keep it in one function.
PARTIAL_WITH_DISCLOSURE hands off WITH the disclosure attached (MT-123 edge); the validator payload must surface the disclosure prominently so partial work cannot masquerade as complete.

The closure API is also the entry point for orchestrator-driven validation (Path A): the orchestrator's spawn-tool-launched validator ultimately reports through the same apply_validation_closure, so both paths converge on identical receipts and state transitions.

Injection posture: the implementer's signal text (notes, evidence summaries) is worker-generated content entering a validator prompt — compose it in delimited data sections after role/output-format sections (same discipline as MT-122 CTRL-5), and run it through the WP's injection-scan seam before ingestion where that seam exists.
Do not block the event-bus thread: handoff work (spawn/notify) runs async off the subscription, with failure of the handoff action itself recorded as an event + open receipt (never silently dropped).

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless handoff plumbing; validation status becomes operator-visible on the board MT MT-125.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Internal lifecycle stage; UserManual coverage lands with MT-125 (board) and MT-126 (end-to-end loop behavior).

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.obligation: Handoff + closure receipts (ids, hashes, actors, timestamps) are queryable machine state; open-receipt = handoff in flight.
Events on the swarm bus/FR path for handoff issued, validator spawned/notified, closure applied, and handoff-action failure.
Deferred to MT-125 (validation status column + open-receipt indicator); recorded here as the consuming surface.

risk_if_missed: The loop dead-ends at READY_FOR_VALIDATION — implemented work piles up unvalidated or the operator hand-relays verdicts, exactly the routing/verdict/closeout friction WP-017 exists to remove.

risks: RISK-1: The implementer's own signal closes the run (self-validation) — a worker could VALIDATE its own work by emitting a second signal.
RISK-2: Duplicate handoff triggers spawn two validators or double-notify, wasting lanes and producing conflicting verdicts.
RISK-3: Auto-spawned validator loops: validator run itself enters the MT lifecycle and spawns another validator, recursing.
RISK-4: Worker-authored signal text injected into the validator prompt steers the validator to PASS (prompt-injection via evidence/notes).
RISK-5: A handoff action failure (notification undeliverable, spawn refused by caps) is swallowed — run sits in VALIDATION_HANDOFF invisibly forever.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): apply_validation_closure rejects a closure whose actor session_id equals the implementer session_id (typed SelfValidationRefused) — tested.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): at-most-one handoff per run via MT-123 single-entry invariant + receipt-existence dedupe — duplicate-event test.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): validator spawns are tagged validation_of=run_id and are NOT MT dispatches — they never open an mt_runs row; asserted by test.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): worker content confined to delimited data sections after composer-owned role/output sections; injection-scan seam invoked where present; validator role overlay instructs verdict-from-evidence, not from implementer claims.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): handoff-action failures emit a typed failure event + leave an open receipt surfaced to MT-125; no silent drop — negative test with a failing sink.

research_provenance.source: WP-017 stub research basis (Claude Code TaskCompleted/SubagentStop hook-notification pattern; Anthropic multi-agent orchestrator-worker + LLM-as-judge evaluator pattern) + operator repo-gov workflow (per-MT WP_VALIDATOR step, receipts both directions per governance receipt discipline) + verified product code: coordinator spawn path, events.rs sinks.
corrections: Validator verdict rides the same hsk.mt_signal@1 schema with a DECLARED role-contextual mapping (no separate verdict schema in v1) — recorded explicitly so a future hsk.validation_verdict@1 upgrade has one seam to replace.
Validator blocker signals map the run to BLOCKED (resolvable), not FAILED — validation-impossible is not validation-rejected.
